decisions.statement: A page body written here parses.
A source, a seat and a date whose day names no export leave every line for that day unwritten.
Whether a day names an export is answered by the page owning export names.
A page that could not be composed is kept as a refusal rather than thrown.
A line is written after the call that wrote the line has returned.
A caller that must lose no line waits on the flush before going down.
Nothing waits on the flush during ordinary work.
A log source page is written where no page names that log source.
A day names its source as an address, and its slug names that source bare.
A log day page is written where no log day page names that day.
A day's page sits in a folder of its own.
A day's folder is named for the day.
A day's lines sit in the day's folder.
A day whose page is already flat keeps that page rather than taking a second.
The parts of a day's lines are named beside the page that day's appender opened.
A body written here names its page type from the root rather than by a relative path.
A page type written here is reached by the id it keeps rather than by its slug.
No page body written here says an id.
A page goes up through the change that works out the kind of path it is handed.
A page's id is worked out by that change rather than by the landing.
A page is written by the change writing a body at a path rather than by an edit composed here.
A landing is believed only after the written file is read off the disk.
A line is appended only after the pages that line sits under have landed.
A landing that refused leaves every line for that day unwritten.
Which part a line goes in is settled as the line arrives.
The queued write decides no part.
A line goes to the highest part already there.
A line goes to the first part where no part is there.
A gap in the parts leaves the parts past the gap unwritten.
A line that would take a part past the entry ceiling opens the next part.
One queue keeps the lines in the order the writing calls came.
A writer whose line names a new date opens the log day for that date.
A refusal is kept and answered rather than thrown.
Nothing here has the calling thread while a line is written.
A day whose first part could not be named leaves every line for that day unwritten.
The folder a page written here sits in is answered from that page's type rather than spelled.
A writer refused by a line that could not reach its part writes again once that page moves.
A writer that is refused looks for its page on every line rather than once a second.

definition: a seat's log lines appended to the log day page the date of each line names
